newsitem.title: SWEDEN: U.S. buyers seen trading Ericsson higher.
newsitem.headline: U.S. buyers seen trading Ericsson higher.

text.p: U.S. investors are seen driving up the share price of Swedish telecommunications group LM Ericsson to a new record high this year, analysts said on Tuesday.

"American investors are buying the share. They love (managing director) Lars Ramqvist's cocky style when he says self-assuredly that Ericsson is the best company in the world," one London-based broker said.
Goran Andersson, Ericsson analyst at Handelsbanken, said he was not surprised by the share's current price.
At 1530 GMT it was trading 7.5 crowns higher at 236.5 crowns, just off its all-time high of 238 crowns.
"Growth in the industry justifies a high price. There is no indication that growth will taper off," Andersoon told Reuters.
The share is difficult to value based on fundamentals, Andersson said.
"The share price is steered by the flow of information (about the company). In 1997 I see several possibilities which can result in some positive information," Andersson said.
But others said the share's value, based on fundamentals, had hit the ceiling.
"Ericsson reached the top a long time ago. It truly is a good company and growth is very good...but the share is extremely highly valued," one analyst said.
U.S. interest was supporting the price, the analyst agreed.
"It is being steered from the U.S.. They like the branch and they like Ericsson. So fundamentals don't play such a big part," the analyst said.
Investors may be fickle toward the share, however.
"The share price is extremely volatile and when another sector becomes hotter, investors will move out. Then the price can quickly fall to 130 crowns just like we saw last summer," the analyst said.
Analysts say that Ericsson's growth will continue in 1997, and the group's turnover could increase by between 20 to 25 billion crowns this year.
Several new markets could emerge for the company while traditional ones are seen continuing to grow.
"The U.S. market is going to take off in 1997 with the launch of the PCS network. In addition, India, Brazil and Spain could become high growth markets," Andersson said.
But at least one analyst was particularly pessimistic.

"The Ericsson share is overall too highly valued and the market has false hopes about it as a growth company. It will just take one piece of bad new to sink the whole ship. And it can go fast," the analyst said.
